The radiation level is a "record" insofar as it's the highest level ever recorded. However, it was what was predicted - some fuel melt through the RPV was expected, and the radiation levels are a confirmation of that.

(Aside. The radiation wasn't even "measured" using instruments. Basically, the scientists said "if the radiation level is X, the robot will survive for Y minutes." IIRC the radiation level has an uncertainty of +/- 30%)

Second, destruction of the walkway grating was also expected due to melt-through... nothing new here either. That grating is just a place to stand on (not that I've enjoyed being undervessel). Below the grating are the drywell sumps, and several feet of concrete until you reach the drywell shell (steel). Total destruction of the undervessel concrete is not expected at U2, because the expected amount of melt-through is (relatively...) small. (That's confirmed by the intact undervessel components.) Plus TEPCO restored injection, so the injected water would also leak out and cool the concrete-corium mix.

U1 on the other hand, where the entire core is expected to have melted through... heavy concrete damage is likely, but total destruction is unlikely since TEPCO also managed to restore injection.
